headline: OpenAI sued by British Columbia over failure to report Tumbler Ridge shooter's chats
summary: The lawsuit alleges OpenAI designed an unsafe product and was negligent for not alerting authorities about the shooter's conversations, which human reviewers had flagged.
details: The Canadian province of British Columbia has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing the company of negligence for not notifying authorities about the Tumbler Ridge shooter's chats. The suit claims the shooting could have been prevented if OpenAI had heeded its human reviewers' advice to alert the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

Reports in February indicated OpenAI failed to alert authorities after employees flagged the shooter's account in 2025 for potential real-world violence warnings. Although the initial account was banned, the shooter created a second account, which OpenAI later discovered.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman issued an apology for not alerting authorities when the first account was banned, and the company committed to notifying authorities about credible threats. However, British Columbia Premier David Eby called Altman's apology "necessary, and yet grossly insufficient."

British Columbia's Attorney General Niki Sharma emphasized that no company should be exempt from accountability due to new technology. The lawsuit was filed in California, OpenAI's home state, potentially leading to larger payouts for victims' families.

In addition to financial compensation, British Columbia seeks for OpenAI to fund the construction of a new school in Tumbler Ridge. OpenAI also faces a separate negligence complaint filed by the victims' families themselves.

headline_marked: [[Full-duplex AI voice agent built]] for Shopify/D2C stores, tackling real-time support challenges
headline: Full-duplex AI voice agent built for Shopify/D2C stores, tackling real-time support challenges
summary: This agent aims to overcome the clunkiness of traditional text chatbots by offering ultra-low latency and interruption handling for natural voice conversations.
details: Traditional text-only chatbots for e-commerce often lead to customer drop-offs and delayed issues. SupportAI was developed as a full-duplex, low-latency AI Voice Agent to handle real-time customer conversations over voice calls.

Full-duplex voice is challenging due to the need for ultra-low latency, enabling natural conversational turn-taking within an 800ms response window. This differs significantly from slower Speech-To-Text (STT) -> LLM -> Text-To-Speech (TTS) pipelines.

The agent also features interruption handling (barge-in), allowing the AI to instantly stop and listen if the customer speaks while it's talking. It also integrates e-commerce context for dynamic actions like checking order status or recovering abandoned carts.

Users can test the full-duplex voice agent live in their browser without signing up. The developer is seeking feedback on current voice AI implementations and desired e-commerce integrations like Shopify or WooCommerce.
